annotations.title: Send a new version of the web app

description: Builds the web app or site in this project with its own framework's command and sends it as a new version. Ploa knows Expo (npx expo export --platform web), Next.js with output: 'export', Astro, SvelteKit with adapter-static, Nuxt (generate), React Router in SPA mode, Angular, Gatsby, Docusaurus, VitePress, Eleventy, Vite, Create React App, Vue CLI, Hugo, Jekyll, MkDocs, Flutter (flutter build web), any project with a build script, and plain HTML; it installs the packages first when they're missing, and finds the output folder (out, dist, build, .output/public, build/web...). A project set up to run a server (Next without output: 'export', Astro's server output, SvelteKit's server adapters, Remix with SSR) is refused with how to make it static: Ploa hosts static files for now. build: false sends what's built already (pass dir for the built folder). Ploa numbers it (the version from app.json or package.json, and a build number it counts), checks it (every file it asks for, no keys or .env, no form sending a password elsewhere, the room, phones, sharing, the PWA's manifest and the store links), and puts it at its own testing address (<site>--<build>.ploa.app) for the site's testers. Nothing goes live: ploa_web_release does, once the person says it's good. Files like .env, .git and node_modules are never sent. The site's own rules go in a ploa.json beside package.json (or in the built folder): rewrites ({from: '/he/*', to: '/he.html'}), redirects, headers (Content-Security-Policy, Cache-Control and a few more) and a proxy sending a path to the site's own API ({from: '/api/*', to: 'https://api.example.com', strip: true}), which Ploa allows only to a domain connected and proven with ploa_web_domain_add.

build.description: Build it first with its framework's command (default true); false sends what's built already.

dir.description: The app's folder (absolute path). Defaults to the folder the agent runs in.

note.description: What this version is, shown in its history (a change, a commit message).

site.description: The site's address (the part before .ploa.app) or ID. Needed when the workspace has more than one site.

version.description: Its version, when the project doesn't say (1.4.1).

name: ploa_web_build
title: Send a new version of the web app
